output.interpretation: The patch refactors app/db.py to replace full table scans with parameterized SQL queries, significantly reducing latency. Validation passed with 0 semantic mismatches and 100% success rate across 6000 operations. The candidate median latency (0.589 ms) is 87.8% lower than the parent (4.644 ms), exceeding the epsilon threshold for acceptance. Per-operation analysis shows consistent improvements: get (0.424 vs 4.073 ms), delete (0.367 vs 4.006 ms), add (0.509 vs 3.964 ms), update (0.517 vs 8.247 ms), and list_search (0.664 vs 4.187 ms). The implementation correctly handles tag filtering via JSON string matching and preserves API contract semantics. Noise levels are low (CV 0.73%), indicating stable performance. The runner accepted the change based on this substantial improvement.
limitations: Tag filtering uses LIKE on JSON strings, which may be slower than native JSON functions on large datasets.
Performance benefits assume non-trivial dataset sizes; overhead may outweigh gains for very small tables.
No index on tags column; complex tag queries rely on sequential scans of the tags text field.
Validation coverage limited to functional correctness; edge cases in concurrent access or extreme input sizes are not measured.
